ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for /v1/generate (streaming). p99=3.8s (SLO=2.0s), p95=1.4s. Trigger=latency-tail-detector at 2026-05-03T09:08:54Z. Paging symptoms: increased disk read IOPS and streaming stalls.

ryan (on-call): taking pager. Can someone post recent deploys or config flips in the last 30m? Also set channel to incident. 

maya harris: we started a kv prefix hashing change at 09:02 UTC under rollout id "prefix-repartition-2026-05-03". Primary diffs: hash function swap (fnv64 -> xxh3-64), and I mistakenly reduced kv.prefix_bucket_ttl from 600s -> 90s when iterating locally. I pushed both in the same rollout.

jeff wong: runtime side: lots of `KV_CACHE MISS` on prefix keys, then origin fetches causing ~400-700ms spikes per token. Streaming connector logs show `stream stalled` and many reconnects. Example snippet:
```
[09:06:17.120] KV_CACHE MISS key="/chat/sess/0a1b" shard=11
[09:06:17.622] origin.fetch latency=510ms
[09:06:18.031] stream: stall session=0a1b
```

sophia - ml infra: current telemetry: aggregate prefix_hit_rate fell from 90% -> 12% over 8m. Shard hotness skewed heavily (some shards <3% hit). Paging IOPS doubled on nodes serving those shards, CPU increased ~30%. Looks consistent with fast TTL + hash remap causing cold re-writes and evictions.

amanda - customer-ops: impact: two customer accounts (both paid) reported user-facing stalls and one issued a support ticket. Preparing an external status update and outbound notice.

ryan (on-call): mitigation plan (fast path):
- Pause rollout: `redwoodctl rollout pause prefix-repartition-2026-05-03`
- Re-apply safe TTL: `redwoodctl config set kv.prefix_bucket_ttl=600 --env=prod`
- If that doesn't bring p99 <2s within 5m, route streaming traffic to `streaming-low-latency-path` to avoid cold-origin hops.
- Notify affected customers proactively.

maya harris: pausing rollout now...

ops-bot: rollout prefix-repartition-2026-05-03 paused by maya.harris at 2026-05-03T09:11:02Z

infra-bot: config change: kv.prefix_bucket_ttl set to 600 by sophia at 2026-05-03T09:12:11Z (no restart required).

jeff wong: observing partial recovery: prefix_hit_rate moving 12% -> 50% in last 3m, but shard skew persists. p99 dropped 3.8s -> 2.4s. Some shards still showing <20% hit.

sophia - ml infra: options to accelerate recovery:
- Run `prefix-repopulate` background job to re-warm hot prefixes onto correct shards (low risk).
- Temporarily enable hotspot replication for top-n prefixes to replicate across 3 shards.
- Apply routing fallback for streaming to drain clients off cold-cache path.

ryan (on-call): prefer harmless warming first + routing fallback if p99 stays above SLO. Jeff, can you kick the rewarm job?

jeff wong: launching `prefix-repopulate --targets=hot-keys --rate=200/s` at 09:18 UTC. Monitoring logs and origin traffic.

amanda - customer-ops: external status: "Investigating elevated streaming latency for some customers. Mitigations underway. Next update in 20 minutes." Sent emails to affected customers with incident id RW-INC-2026-0460.

jeff wong: rewarm job metrics: keys warmed: 14k, origin fetchs backoff reduced, hit rate improving to ~72% after 6m. p99 now 1.9s.

maya harris: root cause summary for post-incident: two coupled changes shipped in same rollout (hash fn swap + accidental TTL shrink). The TTL shrink is the immediate cause of eviction; hash swap exacerbated distribution skew during transition window.

sophia - ml infra: follow-ups I recommend:
- Gate hash function rollouts behind a canary test that monitors prefix_hit_rate and shard-skew for at least 10m at 5% traffic.
- Add a config validator preventing TTL decreases >50% without explicit approval and a warning prompt.
- Create an automated rewarm job that can be invoked by on-call when prefix_hit_rate delta >20%.

ryan (on-call): handoff: jeff will continue remediation monitoring and run a full rebalancer if needed. Maya will own postmortem and rollout guard changes. I'll stay on pager-backoff and monitor customer comms.

jeff wong: scheduling rebalancer `kv-rebalance --mode=gradual --window=30m` at 09:45 UTC to normalize shard distribution. Also adding dashboards for per-shard hit rate and TTL anomalies.

amanda - customer-ops: streamly (customer) confirms responsiveness returned to normal after rewarm. No further reconnects reported.

ops-bot: incident RW-INC-2026-0460 created and assigned to maya.harris, jeff.wong, sophia.ml-infra at 2026-05-03T09:27:00Z

maya harris: will draft postmortem including exact commands, timeline, and remediation: rollout gates, TTL safety checks, and automated rewarm/playbook. Target: postmortem published by EOD 2026-05-05.

ryan (on-call): final metrics at 09:32 UTC: p99=1.5s, p95=0.9s, prefix_hit_rate aggregate=88%, shard skew normalized. Marking as mitigated; switching to monitoring. If we see regression reopen. Thanks everyone :pray:

ops-bot: channel archived by ops-bot at 2026-05-03T10:05:11Z
